class.name: NetwSceneHandle
class.brief_description: The scene an entity belongs to, reached as [member NetwEntity.scene].
class.description: The view a game holds for one scene. It answers who is in it, who it reaches, and when that changes. It holds no authoritative state, so it can be reconstructed at any moment. One scene has one handle, so [code]==[/code] returns "the same scene" and a listener connected through any route hears every edge. Reach it with [method Netw.scene] or [member NetwEntity.scene]. Never [code]null[/code] for an entity in a session. An entity that declares itself a scene resolves to itself, and any other entity resolves to its nearest scene ancestor. Ask [member is_declared] when the difference matters. [b]A scene reaches a player for a reason, and there are two of them.[/b] A body of theirs residing here is one, so parenting a player in is the whole of it and no call follows. A [method watch] is the other, and it is the one for a player with no body here at all. The two are independent and the scene keeps replicating until the last of them is gone, so [method unwatch] does not evict a player still standing in the room. A player may hold as many scenes at once as the game gives them reasons for. [codeblock] lobby.watch(player) arena.add_child(Netw.spawn_player(player, make_player)) lobby.unwatch(player) [/codeblock] Reaching a player is scene-wide and it is not the last word on any one node. [NetwInterestLayer] still filters entity by entity inside a scene this player reaches, so a scene arriving does not mean everything in it arrived. [b]Putting a body somewhere[/b] Three calls move a body and they differ in what they answer, not in where the body lands. Only the last carries a [NetwPromise]. [codeblock lang=text] arena.add_child(body) a first placement. there is nothing to await body.reparent(other) an ordinary Godot move, taken here and replicated. it answers nothing Netw.reparent(body, other) the same move carrying a NetwPromise, which resolves once the session authority holds the body under its new parent [/codeblock] Only [method Netw.reparent] can be awaited, so a game that has to know the session took the move takes that one, and it holds the law with the carry window included. A view resolves its session through the branch its scene node sits in, so a scene whose container is not in the tree returns [member is_declared] [code]false[/code] and every other member empty. [NetwMultiplayer] keeps the same surface keyed by [RID] for callers that already hold one, and [member entity] is the bridge to it: [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_get_bodies], [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_watch] and [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_observe] are the flat spellings of [member bodies], [method watch] and the signals here.

method.name: is_watching
method.description: Whether this scene currently replicates to [param player], for any reason at all. A body of theirs residing here is a reason, and so is a watch [method watch] placed. This answers the effective question, so it stays [code]true[/code] after [method unwatch] while a body of theirs is still standing in the scene.

method.name: observe
method.description:
Calls [param callback] whenever this scene gains or loses a subject of [param event], one of [enum NetwMultiplayer.SceneEvent]. Registering the same [param callback] for the same [param event] twice does nothing. [b]The callback is handed the subject as the object a game holds, never as the internal handle the scene book keys its rows by.[/b] That is the one place this class does more than forward: [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_observe] hands a raw subject straight through, and a game writing this signature would have to name an [RID] it can do nothing with. [codeblock] arena.observe(NetwMultiplayer.SCENE_EVENT_BODY, on_car_edge)
func on_car_edge(present: bool, car: NetwEntity) -> bool: reshuffle(car) return false # true drops the subscription [/codeblock] [constant NetwMultiplayer.SCENE_EVENT_VIEWER] carries a [NetwPlayer]; [constant NetwMultiplayer.SCENE_EVENT_BODY] and [constant NetwMultiplayer.SCENE_EVENT_ENTITY] carry a [NetwEntity]. Returning [code]true[/code] from the callback withdraws it, exactly as the flat verb's does, and [method unobserve] withdraws it by name.

method.name: unobserve
method.description: Withdraws the [param callback] a [method observe] call registered for [param event]. It must be the same [Callable] that was passed to [method observe], because that is the name the relay is filed under; a fresh [Callable] over the same method is a different name and withdraws nothing.

method.name: unwatch
method.description: Withdraws the watch [method watch] placed, so this scene stops replicating to [param player] once nothing else keeps them here. A watch is one reason among several. Withdrawing it does not evict a player whose body is still in this scene, which is what stops a lobby leaving a game to also blind the player it left behind. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the watch is withdrawn ┠╴ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER a null player, or one this session no longer holds ┖╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST this player was not watching [/codeblock] [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: watch
method.description: Replicates this scene to [param player] for as long as the watch stands, without giving them a body in it. Watching is not exclusive and not a move. A player may watch several scenes at once, and watching this one withdraws nothing elsewhere, which is what an avatarless lobby and a spectator both need. [codeblock] Netw.scene(lobby).watch(who) [/codeblock] A scene nested inside another arrives with the scene roots it hangs from, because a watcher cannot hold a node whose parent it has never seen. Those roots arrive as structure alone. Their own content stays with the players they already reach, so watching an inner scene never reveals what sits beside it in the outer one. Idempotent, and refused for a player this session no longer holds, so a handle kept across a disconnect cannot seat whoever reconnected onto that peer id. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the watch stands ┠╴ERR_UNAUTHORIZED this peer is not the server ┠╴ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER a null player, or one this session no longer holds ┖╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST this scene names no live node [/codeblock] [b]Server Only.[/b]

members.member: Every entity standing in this scene, as the [NetwEntity] each one is read through. [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_get_entities] returns the same set under the flat spelling, as the internal handles the session keys its rows by; this member resolves each one so a caller never holds an [RID] it would only hand straight back.

The resolved scene's entity RID, or an invalid RID outside a session. Resolution is self-inclusive and walks the parent-entity chain, so it follows the tree and self-heals on reparent without anything re-enrolling the entity. This is the identity every [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_find]-family verb works on, and the bridge from the entity sugar to the flat surface.

Whether a scene resolved at all. [code]false[/code] for an entity outside every scene, where every other member reads empty. The session-keyed read for a resolved scene is [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_is_declared] over [member entity].
The name this scene was declared under, which is the name [method Netw.scene] and [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_find] resolve.
Every body in this scene that this peer represents, which is empty for a peer with no body here and holds more than one where a game gave it several.

Every player this scene currently replicates to, whether a body of theirs stands here or a [method watch] put them here. A player is a person in the session; a body is the entity they steer, and [member bodies] returns those.
Every body in this scene, in no declared order. A body leaves this array in the call that despawned it, not in the frame its node is freed.

The authored node this scene was declared on, which is the scene's own identity, or [code]null[/code] outside a session. This is the node a game parents content under and reparents players into. [method Netw.spawn] returns [member world] rather than this node when the scene declared [method NetwSceneConfig.isolated], so a caller that spawned an isolated scene reads the root back through here.

The [SubViewport] the framework inserted above [member root] to give this scene a [World2D] and [World3D] of its own, or [code]null[/code] for a scene that shares the session's world. Only a [Viewport] owns a world in Godot, so [method NetwSceneConfig.isolated] is delivered by inserting one rather than by a flag on the authored root. It carries no scene identity of its own and every materializing peer inserts the same one.

signal.name: viewer_entered
signal.description: Emitted when this scene starts replicating to [param player], after the boundary is written, so a listener reading [member viewers] sees them. This reports delivery, not arrival. A body standing here and a [method watch] both raise it and it cannot say which, so a game that spawns players uses [signal NetwSessionHandle.scene_changed] instead.

signal.name: viewer_left
signal.description: Emitted when this scene stops replicating to [param player], whether the last body of theirs left it, a watch was withdrawn, or the membership ended.

signal.name: body_entered
signal.description: Emitted when [param body] joins this scene's roster. A join changes what every other body in the scene is compared against, so a listener that maintains per-body state rebuilds the whole roster here rather than only the newcomer.

signal.name: body_left
signal.description: Emitted when [param body] leaves this scene's roster.
